SecuVidyra Academy

Practical VAPT Foundations

For beginners with basic computer skills and junior IT staff.
10 weeks: 40 live hours + 40 guided practice hours
Outcome: demonstrate skills through lab evidence and an individual submission.

Proposed schedule. Dates, fees and mode to be confirmed.

Learning modules:

Security testing lifecycle

Scope and authorise the work.
Discover assets and assess exposure.
Validate findings with minimal impact.
Report, remediate and retest.



Scope and rules of engagement

List exact hosts, applications and test accounts.
Define exclusions, rate limits and stop conditions.
Record an escalation contact and evidence rules.



Network foundations

IP addresses identify interfaces within a network.
Ports distinguish services on a host.
DNS maps names to records.
A firewall controls traffic according to rules.



Linux and Windows evidence

Identify the operating system and current account.
Inspect service configuration and permissions.
Record timestamps and command outputs.
Use least privilege for routine work.



HTTP request and response

A request contains a method, path, headers and optional body.
A response carries a status, headers and content.
Cookies can carry session identifiers.
TLS protects transport, not application authorisation.



Attack surface inventory

Record host, service, purpose and owner.
Separate public exposure from internal access.
Track assumptions and unresolved assets.



Scanner findings and validation

Treat scanner output as a lead.
Check affected configuration and reachable conditions.
Document evidence supporting or rejecting the finding.
Keep validation within agreed impact limits.



Authentication and access control

Authentication establishes identity.
Authorisation decides permitted actions.
Test role boundaries using separate lab accounts.
Check both data access and privileged functions.



Input handling weaknesses

Untrusted input can cross a trust boundary.
Parameterised queries separate SQL data from instructions.
Context-aware output encoding helps prevent script injection.



Configuration and secrets

Remove unnecessary services and default accounts.
Restrict administrative interfaces.
Keep secrets outside source code and shared reports.
Verify secure defaults after changes.



Risk and business impact

Explain the affected asset and required access.
Describe a plausible business consequence.
Separate technical severity from remediation priority.
Record limitations and uncertainty.



Evidence and report structure

Include scope, method and limitations.
For each finding: condition, evidence, impact and fix.
Redact tokens and personal data.
Record report version and reviewer.



Retest and closure

Repeat the original permitted test after the fix.
Check related roles or paths for regression.
Mark fixed, partially fixed, open or not retested.
Retain evidence and client acceptance.



Capstone

Assess a fictional small-business lab within a signed scope.
Submit an asset list, test log and three validated findings or justified clean checks.
Deliver a short report and one retest record.

All testing takes place on assigned authorised labs with synthetic data.

Academy completion certificate only. No employment guarantee.
